evidence.source: Qiu Yansui, “從漢語詞族看上古聲母的擬音問題,” 國文學報 48 (2010), pp. 219–254
evidence.field: section 7 父聲系、巴聲系, printed pp. 245–246 (PDF pp. 26–27)
evidence.text: Qiu groups 父 and 巴 sound-series material for discussion and writes that 爸, which gets its sound from 巴, is a later graph for 父. He lists 巴-series readings including 爸 with fanqie 必駕切 and 捕可切, and discusses the broader historical relationship between the 父 and 巴 sound series. This is a scholarly account about the lexical/phonological relation and sound-series history; it does not establish when the graphic compound 父+巴 was first formed. It differs in emphasis from the simple component account “父 meaning + 巴 sound,” so retain the attributed distinction instead of presenting the accounts as identical.
evidence.title: 從漢語詞族看上古聲母的擬音問題

evidence.text: The entry transmits the Shuowen explanation of 父 as a family head who leads and teaches, formed from 又 holding a staff. This is evidence for the historical account of 父 and its father sense; it does not establish the date or formation of 爸.

evidence.text: The inspected entry explicitly analyzes 爸 as a phono-semantic compound: semantic 父 and phonetic 巴. It reports Zhengzhang Old Chinese 巴 *praː and 爸 *praːs, *baʔ. These are values in Zhengzhang’s system, not Baxter–Sagart readings; the entry does not recover the original name or referent of 巴.

gaps: No consulted source provides a securely dated physical witness for the earliest complete 爸 graph. The MOE page reports absence from Shuowen and cites earlier dictionary references, but the cited entries’ physical witnesses were not inspected here.

The formation analysis remains attributed: MOE confirms the present graphic composition 父 above 巴; Wiktionary reports 父 as semantic and 巴 as phonetic; Qiu describes 爸 as a later graph for 父 and discusses the associated sound series. These accounts do not by themselves establish when the graph was composed or settle the spoken word’s full lexical history.

The original referent/name of 巴 remains uncertain in the inspected sources. A phonetic role in 爸 and the reported historical readings do not independently identify the object depicted by early 巴 forms.

The packet’s Proto-Sino-Tibetan proposal and claim that 爸 preserves an older pronunciation of 父 were not independently established in this research. Do not treat this lexical-origin proposal as whole-graph borrowing or as proof of 巴’s phonetic role.

No Baxter–Sagart comparison is provided: the relevant local TSV was absent, and the inspected pages did not establish exact Baxter–Sagart rows for both 巴 and 爸. Do not mix Zhengzhang reconstructions with Baxter–Sagart notation.
